Commentary.Commentary: Okay! 6th Women's WT20 final. 5th featuring Australia. Boy, did they come up in fine form. They now wait their competitors in the winner of the second semi-final between India and England. Do join us for that in a while. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Victorious Australian captain, Meg Lanning, says that she is relieved and happy with the win. Stresses that the Aussies were ready for this game and played well. Admits that the conditions were tough and adds that they wanted the first two wickets quickly with the ball, to put pressure on the middle order. Believes that the Aus batters did well not to panic as they knew that they bat very deep. Praises Rachael Haynes for her cameo.

Windies skipper, Stafanie Taylor, defends her ploy to bowl first on this track, in spite of the loss. Feels that the Windies bowled poorly in the last 6 overs but even then, reckons 143 was chaseable and puts the defeat down to poor shot-making. Says that it was one of those days where no one got going. Thanks the crowd for coming out in large numbers to support and apologizes for the poor finish.

ALYSSA HEALY HAS BEEN NAMED THE PLAYER OF THE MATCH. Smiles on being asked whether she was frustrated on not being able to bat against India. Denies that and says that she used that time to recuperate well. On the pitch, she admits that it was a bit difficult to bat on and the batters needed to graft it out. On wearing glasses in the field, Healy says that she has been wearing spectacles for the last 6 months but tonight was the first time she wore it on the field. Does not want to take this win as a revenge of the 2016 WT20 final and says that the Aussies were desperate to get into the final. Thanks the crowd for coming in large numbers. On being asked whether she would stick around to watch the second semi-final, Alyssa smiles and says that probably the Aussies need to celebrate and enjoy this win right now.

If you were to be told, that 3-0-14-1 would be the most expensive figures of the innings, how would your reaction be? Outstanding bowling display from Australia. Yes, the Windies got succumbed into self-created pressure but that does not take away anything from the Women In Yellow. Ellyse Perry set it up with a frugal spell while Kimmince and Gardner then ran through the rest, with combined figures of 8-0-32-4. Please stay tuned for the presentation...

143 was not going to be the easiest of chases, no doubt but the Windies needed a bit of smart cricket to start. They backed themselves for some power-hitting in the Powerplay and score quick runs when the ball was new - but Perry's spell - 2-1-2-2 stung them. They barely recovered after that, losing wickets one after the other. Just the captain managed double figures, which indicates a sorry figure.
Unbelievable. A match totally unworthy of being a semi-final. Did Windies lose it at the toss itself? Or were Australia just too good in terms of applying themselves on a tricky pitch?

OUT! STUMPED! AUSTRALIA ENTER THE FINAL! The Windies have been dug out of their misery. Floated outside off, Selman jumps out and has a heave-ho. Does not connect. Healy collects and connects. AUSTRALIA WIN BY 71 RUNS!
Full and down the leg side, played straight to square leg.
Outside off, Selman looks to steer it through the off side but misses.
Georgia Wareham returns. 1-0-7-0 so far.
Full and outside off, slapped down to long on for another single.
Pushes this through mid on for one.
DROPPED! Nearly the final wicket. Outside off, SC swings hard but gets a top edge. Ellyse Perry runs to her left from deep mid-wicket but cannot hold on. Two runs taken.
Short and wide outside off, Shamilia looks to cut but misses.
Outside off, driven through the covers for a run,
Full and outside off, Connell looks to sweep but the ball goes off the inner half of the bat through square leg. A single results.
Delissa Kimmince is back. 3-0-11-2 so far. Can she finish it off with a 3-fer?
Gets across and swats it down to long off for one more. Spectacular spell from Gardner - 4-0-15-2.
Full and outside off, chipped down to long off for a run.
Outside off, dragged to long on for a single.
Outside off, Selman jumps out and tries to flick but the ball goes off her pads to point. A leg bye taken.
WIDE. Down the leg side, left alone.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Shakera Selman in the last batter in.
OUT! BOWLED! You miss, I hit. A length ball, angling into the stumps, Fletcher swings but misses. Crash. Sound of timber.
Outside off, a swing and a miss.
Shamilia Connell is in at number 10, replacing Henry.

OUT! One more. The Windies are simply not able to read the pitch. Landed outside off, Henry looks to go over cover but the bat comes early, the ball comes late and the mismatch results in a miscue to Georgia Wareham at mid off.
WIDE. Miles outside off, Henry goes after it but misses.
Outside off, looks to punch but gets a bottom edge to cover. A single taken.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a run.
Landed outside off, Henry looks to cut but then bails out, looking at the away movement. Excellent diving take by Healy.
Megan Schutt is back. 2-0-9-0 so far.
Short and outside off, flayed through point for a single.
Stays back in the crease and blocks.
One more outside off, a play and a miss.
Full and around off, Henry looks to flick but gets a leading edge back to the bowler.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Full and outside off, pushed in front of cover for a run.
Down the leg side, helped through square leg for a single.
Full and outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Who's in next to face the music? Afy Fletcher.

OUT! Caught again. Number 7 down. This is turning out to be a very one-sided semi-final. Full and outside off, Cooper gets down and looks to sweep but the bounce does her in. The ball takes the top edge and Healy calls for it and takes it to her left.
Action replay of the previous delivery.
Short and outside off, Cooper misses out on the cut.
Pushes this through the covers for a run.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.
WIDE. Starts off with a real loosener down the leg side.
Delissa Kimmince is back. 2-0-7-1 so far.
Landed outside off, spinning in, past the inside edge and to the keeper's gloves.
Landed outside off, steered straight to short third man.
FOUR! Little bit of fresh air for the hosts. Half volley outside off, pretty wide, driven between mid off and cover.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a quick single.
Outside off, Cooper looks to force this through the off side but gets an inside edge to the leg side.
Chinelle Henry walks in at number 8, replacing Knight.

OUT! Straight to the fielder! This is going haywire for the Windies now. A length ball outside off, Knight swings hard but finds Ellyse Perry stationed at deep mid-wicket! Does not have to move an inch!
Ashleigh Gardner is back too. 1-0-4-0 so far.
Full and outside off, spinning away, watchfully defended. Just a run and a wicket from the over, Molineux' figures read 3-0-14-1!
Full and around middle, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
Outside off, Cooper tries to run it past the keeper but misses.
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
Pushes this through long on for a single.
Britney Cooper walks in at number 7, replacing Taylor.

OUT! Caught! The Windies have lost half their side at nearly the halfway stage. And this one is of their skipper. Floated outside off, Taylor jumps out and wants to go down the ground. But the ball grips off the surface, is delayed in its arrival and goes off the splice of the bat. Simple catch at wide long off for Georgia Wareham.
Sophie Molineux returns. 2-0-13-0 so far.
Full and outside off, heaved straight to mid on.
Landed outside off, Knight goes back and runs it down past the keeper for a couple to third man. The Aussies played plenty of such shots. 99 more needed from 61 balls now.
Goes back and connects this time, punching the ball through the covers for a single.
Short once more, this time the cut is missed.
Dropped short now, Stafanie mistimes her pull to mid-wicket.
FOUR! Welcome boundary for the Windies! Down the leg side, Taylor gets down and sweeps it through fine leg for a boundary!
Georgia Wareham to bowl now. Interesting tactic from Lanning. Thought she might have wanted to continue with her spinners and wrestle more control.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Outside off, a play and a miss. Looked to cut.
Full and around middle, Stafanie looks to flick now but gets a leading edge. Short of cover.
Short and outside off, cut through point for a couple. There is an appeal for a run out but the skipper is home.
Landed outside off, Taylor looks to cut but is done in by the bounce.
Floated miles outside off, steered straight to cover.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers.
Landed outside off, pushed towards point.
Gets across a touch and flicks it through square leg for a run.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
On middle and leg, helped behind square leg for a run.
Full and outside off, eased through the covers for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers for another single.
Down the leg side, worked through square leg for one.
Full and outside off, played through point.
On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a run.
Kycia Knight arrives, at number 6, replacing McLean.

OUT! Gone for a duck! Kimmince strikes second ball. Full and outside off, McLean looks to drive it on the up but that is a no-no on this pitch. The ball holds off the surface and  goes straight to Meg Lanning at short extra cover.
Landed outside off, slapped through point for a single.
Landed outside off, watchfully defended. 26/3 IN THE POWERPLAY FOR THE WINDIES. They need 117 from 84 balls.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Landed outside off, played straight to point.
Full and just outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off again, another play and a miss.
Outside off, cut shot missed.
Natasha McLean comes in at number 5, replacing Campbelle. Megan Schutt returns as well. 1-0-8-0 so far.

OUT! Caught! A soft dismissal and the Windies are three down in the Powerplay! A length ball, around off, Campbelle tries to pull it away but finds Sophie Molineux at short square leg! Second wicket for Perry and her bowling figures read 2-1-2-2!
On middle and leg, hit straight to mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, Campbelle looks to drive but gets it off the inner half back to the bowler.
Outside off, tapped through the covers for a run.
Outside off, a swish and a miss.

DIRECT HIT WOULD HAVE GOT CAMPBELLE. A full toss outside off, Shemaine hits it slightly wide of mid off, sets off for a single, but then slips. However, she continues to run, chancing the arm of Meg Lanning who has a shy at the bowler's end. SC loses her bat too. But the throw misses.
Full and outside off, a quick single taken towards the left of the bowler, in front of cover.

FOUR! Poor line. Down the leg side and deserved to be hit. Fuller in length, Campbelle sweeps it powerfully through fine leg. Short fine leg dives but cannot quite stop the ball, in spite of taking the pace off.
Full and outside off, driven through the covers for one.
Goes back and drags this short ball through mid-wicket for a run.
Pushes this through point for a single.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off again, played towards point once more. A WICKET MAIDEN FROM PERRY!
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Shemaine Campbelle walks in at number 4, replacing Dottin.

OUT! The stumps are a mess! Perry has got her length spot on and won the battle of the all-rounders. She keeps it on a length outside off and gets it to nip back in. Dottin is cramped for room and looks to push it through the off side but is done in by the movement. The ball takes the inside edge and rattles the stumps! And Perry is flying. Exactly what Australia needed upfront.
There is that width, short in length outside off, DD slashes but misses.
Short and outside off, Deandra mistimes her pull to mid on.
Landed outside off, cramping her for room, Dottin looks to punch but gets a bottom edge.
Ellyse Perry into the attack as well.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Stafanie Taylor comes in at number 3, replacing Matthews.

OUT! Brilliant work from Alyssa Healy! Matthews is run out. Outside off, Hayley tries to run it down to third man but gets a bit of a bottom edge. The ball rolls behind and it takes HM a while to understand that she is out of her crease. But no such lack of awareness from Healy. She reacts quickly in a flash and rips off the stumps! It is referred upstairs and replays show that the bat has not even come down onto the ground, let alone be in the crease. Terrific glovework.
Is that a stumping or a run out? Referred upstairs...
Full and down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
FOUR! BELLIGERENT! Short and wide outside off, Dottin cuts it through the covers and finds the gap!
Tossed up a bit wider outside off, Dottin looks to slog but misses.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Sophie Molineux to bowl from the other end.
Full and down the leg side, Hayley misses her flick but the ball runs fine off her pads. Two leg byes taken. 10 runs from the opening over!
FOUR! BANG! There comes the first boundary of the run chase! Short and wide outside off, Matthews flashes a cut and gets it over a leaping Rachael Haynes at point!
Another long off, DD is ready to pull but mistimes it. The ball goes off the bottom edge towards mid on and a quick run is taken.
Short and outside off, dabbed straight to short third man.
Outside off, played straight to point.
ANOTHER WIDE. Fuller and down the leg side again, Deandra misses out on the flick this time.
WIDE. Short and down the leg side, Dottin misses out on the pull.
The Windies are away! Around off, swinging in slightly, Matthews works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Welcome back. 143 needed for a win. Deandra Dottin and Hayley Matthews are the openers. Megan Schutt to bowl first up, to the latter. Here we go!
